The credibility of the evidence in the text is mixed. The written confession itself is direct evidence, but its admissibility is contested by the defense's claim of duress. The supporting evidence for this claim—phone records showing repeated calls from unknown sources—is relevant and credible in establishing a pattern of harassment or pressure, which lends plausibility to the duress argument. However, phone records alone do not prove the content of the calls or that threats were actually made; they only show contact occurred. Therefore, while the evidence is relevant to the legal matter of whether the confession was voluntary, it is circumstantial and requires further corroboration to fully establish the claim of duress.
